subject: general
question: A resistor has a resistivity ρ. This resistor is now cut into three equal parts. The resistivity of each part will be:
solution:
The correct answer is __**ρ**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The resistivity (ρ) of a material is a fundamental property that does not change when the material is cut into smaller pieces.
 
• Resistivity is dependent only on the material itself, not on the dimensions or shape of the resistor.
 
• When a resistor is cut into three equal parts, each part retains the same resistivity as the original resistor.
 
• Therefore, the resistivity of each of the three parts remains ρ.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Resistivity (ρ)**

 
 
• Resistivity is a measure of how strongly a material opposes the flow of electric current.
 
• It is denoted by the Greek letter ρ (rho) and is measured in ohm-meters (Ω·m).
 
 
 
• **Resistance (R)**
 
 
• Resistance is the property of a component that restricts the flow of electric current.
 
• It depends on the material's resistivity, the component's length, and its cross-sectional area.
 
• Formula: R = ρ * (L/A), where L is the length and A is the cross-sectional area.
 
 
 
• **Effect of Cutting a Resistor**
 
 
• When a resistor is cut into smaller pieces, the resistance of each piece changes, but the resistivity remains the same.
 
• The resistance of each piece is determined by its new length and cross-sectional area.
 
 
 
• **Electrical Conductivity**
 
 
• Electrical conductivity is the reciprocal of resistivity and measures a material's ability to conduct electric current.
 
• It is denoted by the Greek letter σ (sigma) and is measured in siemens per meter (S/m).
